Varied ability to get involved in the business.  Ability to have input into North America policies and procedures.  Understand different Fives entities.
I enjoyed the work the that I was doing and the skills that I was applying and learning.

My return position I did not like but not because it was AP but because my time was spent answering emails from Vendors for non payment that was outside of my control.  Also spent fixing a lot of errors that other's had made.

I enjoyed my coworkers and the kind of intricate technical work that we do.

I really enjoyed being able to bring a positive outlook to the safety culture here in the building. I felt people were very receptive to having a full time safety person that they knew would be able to make improvments to things by using a safety mindset. Sometimes you have a "maintenance" issue but really when you look at it, it truly is a "safety" issue. And once we say we have a "safety" issue, we can move more quickly on corrective actions.

my direct reports and I have a great working relationship. There are a few co-workers I will miss.

Varity of the work, the people.

Everything is a rush.  Tough to determine the priority of all the different issues.  You could get in trouble for asking questions if you don't know something.  Micro managing is common.  People here 30 years don't want to make a decision.  They are afraid it might be the wrong one.  Seems like a handful of people make all the decisions.
Planning and managing projects by myself.

Stretched too thin and was unable to really work with the employees to develop and nature their skills within the department.  Thus, not allowing him to truly manage the people but rather hew as managing to scale the projects.

We handle and deal with a vast array of chemicals. I was able to get some exposure monitoring completed to start mitigating some of those exposure hazards, But I feel there is still a lot of opportunities for improvements in that space. As I stated during my interview process, the chemical background I had was not as robust as I would have like it to be and proved challenging for me.

The constant feeling of inadequacy due to lake of training. This led to wondering if I was going to be let go at any moment, or that the management was keeping a record of failure to justify discharge of employment. At minimum, the record would allow them to never compensate monetarily any more than absolutely necessary.
The position could be very stressful. I was considered on call 24/7 and talked to if I didn't answer a call or missed a call. It would have been good to get praise for a job well done.
The overall environment of the plant floor and the age of our production equipment.
Having to constantly be looking work within the department.
